anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > A wave passes, but what travels?: "A floating straw merely bobs up and down as each crest passes."
purpose: Illustrate Leonardo da Vinci's historical observation comparing an advancing wave pattern across a wheat field with rooted stalks bending locally, alongside circular water ripples passing a bobbing floating straw.
what_to_show: A two-panel comparative scientific diagram on a clean white background. Panel A (Wheat field): A field of green wheat stalks rooted in soil. An aerial gust of wind creates an undulating wave crest travelling horizontally from left to right, indicated by a broad green arrow labelled 'wave pattern travels right'. Individual wheat stalks bend forward under the wind and spring back upright, annotated with curved double-headed arrows labelled 'stalks oscillate locally about fixed roots'. Panel B (Pond ripples): Concentric circular ripple rings spreading outward across calm blue water from a central splash, with radial arrows labelled 'ripples expand outward'. A yellow floating straw near the midpoint bobs vertically, with a vertical double-headed arrow labelled 'straw bobs up and down with zero net horizontal travel'.
what_to_notice: Notice that in both panels, the visible pattern travels across space while the individual material elements (rooted wheat stalks and floating straw) undergo only bounded local motion around their resting positions.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > A travelling disturbance through neighbour interactions: "Each section of the rope pulls directly on the neighbouring section next to it."
purpose: Demonstrate wave motion in a stretched rope as a travelling disturbance, showing the causal neighbour-to-neighbour interaction across three successive time snapshots and tracking the local vertical oscillation of a single marked ribbon or point.
what_to_show: A three-step vertical time sequence (t1, t2, t3) of a taut horizontal rope. A red ribbon is tied at a fixed horizontal distance x = 1.0 m from the left end. At t1, an upward pulse approaches from the left; the ribbon rests on the dashed horizontal equilibrium line. At t2, the peak of the pulse reaches x = 1.0 m; the ribbon is lifted to its maximum vertical displacement, with vertical force arrows showing upward pull from the preceding segment and downward restoring tension from the following segment. At t3, the pulse has advanced to the right of x = 1.0 m; the ribbon has returned to its horizontal equilibrium line. A prominent horizontal arrow above the rope indicates 'constant pulse speed v', while a vertical double-headed arrow at the ribbon indicates 'local vertical oscillation'.
what_to_notice: Notice that while the pulse moves steadily to the right across the three snapshots, the marked red ribbon moves exclusively up and down along a vertical line, returning to equilibrium after the pulse passes.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Mechanical demonstrations: ropes, springs, and ripple tanks: "A compressed cluster of coils travels smoothly along the length of the spring."
purpose: Demonstrate wave motion in a helical spring (slinky), showing a travelling compression pulse advancing horizontally while individual marked coils oscillate back and forth parallel to the spring and return to their equilibrium spacing.
what_to_show: A two-time-step horizontal sequence of a stretched helical spring with uniform equilibrium coil spacing. One specific coil near the middle is highlighted in bright orange. In snapshot 1, a hand at the left pushes forward and pulls back, forming a region of tightly compressed coils travelling to the right; the orange coil is just ahead of the compression in its resting position. In snapshot 2, the compression has reached the orange coil, shifting it temporarily to the right, while coils behind it expand back to normal spacing. Double-headed horizontal arrows on the orange coil indicate 'local back-and-forth oscillation', while a long horizontal arrow above the spring indicates 'compression pulse travel'.
what_to_notice: Notice that the compressed region travels along the entire spring, but individual coils shift temporarily along the spring axis and return to their original resting spacing.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Mechanical demonstrations: ropes, springs, and ripple tanks: "A light cork floating on the water surface bobs up and down near one fixed spot."
purpose: Demonstrate wave motion in a ripple tank, showing straight and circular wavefronts spreading from a vibrating source toward an absorber while a floating cork bobs locally about its equilibrium position without drifting across the tank.
what_to_show: A dual-view schematic of a shallow ripple tank. Top view (overhead): A vibrating dipper at the left generates circular or straight wavefronts advancing toward a porous foam absorber at the right, indicated by horizontal wave propagation arrows. A brown circular cork floats in the centre. Side cross-sectional view: An undulating sinusoidal water surface profile at one instant, showing the floating cork perched on the water. A vertical double-headed arrow through the cork indicates 'bobbing motion about equilibrium', and a crossed-out horizontal arrow indicates 'no net horizontal drift'.
what_to_notice: Notice that although the wavefronts travel continuously from the vibrating source to the absorber beach, the floating cork only bobs up and down, demonstrating that water is not transported across the tank.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Progressive waves and energy transfer: "A progressive wave transfers energy from place to place."
purpose: Model the energy transfer pathway of a progressive wave from input work done at an oscillating source, through inter-element interactions in the medium, to mechanical work done on a distant receiver or absorber.
what_to_show: A linear energy-pathway block diagram aligned with a mechanical wave medium. On the left, a box labelled 'Input Source' shows 'Work done on medium' with an input arrow. In the centre, a schematic row of coupled particles shows bidirectional inter-element restoring forces with the annotation 'Kinetic and potential energy passed between neighbours; net particle displacement = 0'. A broad gradient arrow running horizontally beneath the particles is labelled 'Energy transfer: E travelling rightward at wave speed v'. On the right, a box labelled 'Distant Receiver' shows 'Mechanical work done on load (e.g. lifting a cork or moving a bell)'.
what_to_notice: Notice that energy flows continuously in one direction from source to receiver, even though the particles in the intermediate medium undergo zero net transport.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Single pulses and continuous periodic wave trains: "A mechanical vibration generator drives one end of a taut horizontal string."
purpose: Provide authentic examiner evidence showing how Cambridge assesses wave motion on a stretched string connected to a mechanical vibration generator.
what_to_show: Authentic examination apparatus figure from Cambridge paper 9702/21/M/J/24 Question 5 Fig. 5.1 showing a horizontal taut string of length 1.2 m extending from point P to point Q. Point P on the left connects to the vertical vibrating pin of a grey rectangular vibration generator. Point Q on the right is fixed rigidly to a hatched vertical wall. Clear leader lines indicate 'vibration generator', 'string', and 'wall', with a horizontal dimension line labelled '1.2 m'.
what_to_notice: Notice the standard experimental arrangement: the vibration generator at P acts as the continuous oscillating source that does work on the string, sending progressive disturbances along the 1.2 m span toward Q.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Single pulses and continuous periodic wave trains: "The curved string shows the instantaneous displacement of the medium from its straight equilibrium axis."
purpose: Provide authentic examiner evidence showing a progressive or standing wave profile on a string displaced from its dashed horizontal equilibrium axis.
what_to_show: Authentic examination figure from Cambridge paper 9702/21/M/J/24 Question 5 Fig. 5.2 showing a horizontal dashed line connecting point P on the left and point Q on the right, representing the undisturbed equilibrium position of the string. A thick solid sinusoidal curve displays the displaced string at one instant of time, showing crests and troughs intersecting the equilibrium axis.
what_to_notice: Notice that the dashed straight line marks the undisturbed equilibrium position of the string particles. The solid curve shows the instantaneous displacement of each particle above or below equilibrium at one moment in time.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Two-track wave analysis: disturbance speed versus particle speed: "An individual particle on the string moves downwards through its equilibrium position with changing speed."
purpose: Provide authentic examiner evidence showing a straight horizontal string with marked points, illustrating that particles on the string oscillate through their equilibrium position.
what_to_show: Authentic examination figure from Cambridge paper 9702/21/M/J/22 Question 5 Fig. 5.1 showing a straight horizontal line representing a string stretched between fixed points A and B. Six solid black dots are spaced equally along the string. A labelled arrow points down and to the right to point P on the string between the first and second dots, with the caption noting that point P is moving downwards through equilibrium.
what_to_notice: Notice that while the string momentarily passes through a straight horizontal line, point P has a non-zero downward velocity. Individual points on a wave oscillate across equilibrium rather than staying permanently at rest.
